title: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life
hook: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life

beats.caption: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life
Three discoveries hit the journals this week.
beats.narration: Three major science stories dropped this week. But the third one is the big one.

beats.caption: We found 12,000 ancient fossils.
beats.narration: Scientists found over twelve thousand fossils in Australia that are 1.7 billion years old.

beats.caption: Oxygen was the turning point.
beats.detail: Complex cells only survived with it.
beats.narration: It turns out these complex cells had a specific requirement for where they could live.

beats.caption: They lived in coastal mudflats.
beats.narration: They were found everywhere from mudflats to the open ocean, showing where life first took hold.

beats.caption: This creates a clear map of evolution.
beats.narration: This map shows exactly how oxygen availability dictated the rise of complex life forms early on.

beats.caption: It is just one important clue.
beats.detail: We are still piecing the puzzle together.
beats.narration: It is just one piece of a massive puzzle, but it helps explain how life became complex.
